feedback:
Written before this candidate races. The candidate is the iteration 5 baseline (best raced, 417.25: sensors at x = -0.05 to 0.05 and y = 0.07, sensor_size 0.012, kp 1.5, ki 0.5, kd 0.4, last_direction) with one controller change, base_speed 1.2 to 1.0. The line_loss field is already last_direction, so the search_right test from iteration 7 is correctly reverted. Iteration 7 returned identical numbers to iteration 5, so the recovery-mode change had no measurable effect and is not a lever.

What the evidence supports: iterations 0 to 2 showed max_error near 0.061 whatever base_speed, kp or ki was, but iteration 3 showed kd 0.4 cut oval max_error to 0.043 and lifted oval finish to 0.8. Iteration 5 showed forward sensors (y 0.07) doubled s-bend progress (0.28 to 0.56). Iterations 4 and 6 showed the wider x spread (±0.07) and the larger footprint (0.016) both hurt. Slalom has stuck at 1 line-loss event per run with progress near 0.19 across iterations 3 to 7. The stated hypothesis, that the slalom loss is a speed-limited overshoot at bend entry, is plausible and is a clean single-variable test. The oval finished in 1.88 s at base_speed 1.2, so a slower run should still finish inside the 3.0 s limit, but it will lose some time score. The candidate is valid and not obviously broken, and the test is cheap, so I approve it to race for telemetry.

What to do next depends on the race. If slalom progress rises above 0.2 and the oval still finishes at 1.0, keep base_speed 1.0 and step the speed back up cautiously, since the gain shows speed was the limit. If slalom progress is unchanged or lower, speed is not the limit: keep base_speed 1.2 and test kp 1.8 to check whether turn authority is limiting. If the oval finish falls below 0.8, return to base_speed 1.2 and keep the iteration 5 baseline.
requested_changes: If slalom progress rises above 0.2 with base_speed 1.0 and the oval finish stays at 1.0, keep base_speed 1.0 and try base_speed 1.1 to find the speed that balances slalom progress against oval completion time, with all other fields held at iteration 5 values.

If slalom progress is unchanged or lower at base_speed 1.0, return base_speed to 1.2 and test controller.kp 1.8 alone, since iterations 0 to 2 showed kp and speed barely moved max_error and turn authority may be the limit on the slalom.

If the oval finish falls below 0.8 or oval completion time rises above about 2.5 s at base_speed 1.0, revert to base_speed 1.2 and keep the iteration 5 design as the baseline, since iteration 5 showed that design finishes the oval reliably.
